notes: Breadboard hole names follow the catalogue convention (top half = bank 't' rows a-e, bottom half = bank 'b' rows f-j, with f/e next to the centre gap), although the diagram's row letters are printed the other way round. Only the strip (column and half) matters electrically.

Rail holes are estimated from the image: the lower rail pair has the top row as the negative rail (bn) and the bottom row as the positive rail (bp). The exact hole numbers (bp.2, bn.1, bp.11, bn.12, bn.25) are approximate.

In the diagram the potentiometer's two outer legs go in columns 13 and 15 of the bottom half, with VCC on 13 (red jumper to + rail) and GND on 15 (black jumper to - rail). Its wiper goes in column 14 of the top half, which the A5 jumper reads.
The A0 jumper (the DAC output) goes to buzzer leg 1 in column 26, and buzzer leg 2 in column 30 goes through a black jumper to the - rail.
The tutorial text doesn't explain why A5 is wired to the potentiometer wiper. The sketch is assumed to read the pot on A5, even though the A5 label sits next to the A0 and A5 headers.
